newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Tamil party urges Sri Lanka to talk to rebels.
newsitem.headline: Tamil party urges Sri Lanka to talk to rebels.

text.p: A mainstream Tamil party on Monday urged Sri Lanka to end the war against the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) and negotiate peace with the rebels.

"We appeal to the government to put a halt to the ongoing war and to give a boost to the political process. The LTTE should also be included in the political process as their role is important in finding a settlement to the ethnic crises," the afternoon Observer quoted Murugesu Sivasithamparam, leader of the Tamil United National Front (TULF) as saying.
The TULF supports President Chandrika Kumaratunga's ruling People's Alliance government in parliament.

One of its legislators, Arunasalam Thangathurai, and four other people were killed in a grenade attack in the eastern port city of Trincomalee earlier this month. He was the eighth TULF member to be killed in as many years.

Police have blamed the LTTE for Thangathurai's killing, but nobody has claimed responsibility for the attack. Ten suspects have been arrested, and police say there should soon be a breakthrough in investigations.
Sivasithamparam said his party was committed to a peaceful solution to the 13-year-old ethnic war, which the government says has claimed more than 50,000 lives. The LTTE say the toll is higher.
"We have committed ourselves to finding a constructive political solution to the ethnic crisis. Therefore, the gunshots and grenades cannot change our path," he told the newspaper.
The government has proposed constitutional reforms that are being discussed by a parliamentary select committee.
But the process has slowed by differences between Sri Lanka's political parties, including the Tamil parties and the main opposition United National Party.
